❗️🌊🇵🇭 - A 7.6-magnitude tectonic earthquake struck offshore Davao Oriental, Philippines, at 9:43 a.m. local time on Thursday, October 10, 2025. 

The shallow quake, with a depth of 10 kilometers, had its epicenter at 07.07°N, 127.06°E, southeast of the province. 

The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology issued a tsunami warning, forecasting a destructive tsunami with life-threatening wave heights exceeding one meter above normal tides, particularly in enclosed bays and straits. 

The first waves are expected between 9:43 a.m. and 11:43 a.m. and could persist for hours. 

Immediate evacuation to higher ground or inland areas is ordered for coastal regions in Eastern Samar, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, Surigao del Sur, and Davao Oriental. 

Boat owners in these areas should secure vessels and avoid waterfronts, while those at sea must remain in deep waters. 

The Philippines is situated along the Pacific Ring of Fire, a seismically active zone. In response, Davao City has suspended classes.

#BREAKING 🇵🇭7.6 Quake Jolts Southern Philippines, Sparks Tsunami Panic

A powerful 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck offshore near Manay, Davao Oriental, shaking the southern Philippines and triggering widespread tsunami warnings. 
Coastal communities scrambled to evacuate as waves up to 3 meters were forecast, with tremors felt across Mindanao.
The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center extended alerts to Indonesia and Palau, citing hazardous waves within 300 km of the epicenter. 
This comes just weeks after a deadly 6.9-magnitude quake near Cebu claimed 72 lives, underscoring the region’s vulnerability on the volatile Ring of Fire.

data.text:
Evacuation ordered as destructive tsunami looms after Davao quake
.
A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck offshore Davao Oriental at 9:43 a.m. local time on Thursday, prompting a tsunami warning from the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs), according to local media, The Philippines Daily Inquirer. Authorities have warned of life-threatening waves and urged residents in coastal areas to evacuate immediately.
.
The shallow tectonic quake occurred at a depth of 10 kilometres, with its epicentre located at 07.07°N, 127.06°E, southeast of Davao Oriental. Based on local tsunami scenario models, Phivolcs forecasts waves more than one metre above normal tides, particularly in enclosed bays and straits. 
.
The first tsunami waves are expected to arrive between 9:43 a.m. and 11:43 a.m. and may continue for several hours.
.
Residents in Eastern Samar, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte, Surigao del Sur, and Davao Oriental are strongly advised to move to higher ground or further inland. Boat owners have been urged to secure their vessels or remain in deep waters until further notice.
.
The Philippines, situated along the Pacific Ring of Fire, is prone to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, making preparedness a crucial aspect. Authorities continue to closely monitor the situation.
.

From Talk to Action: The Meeting That Brought Hope to Our Farmers

There are moments in governance that go beyond the headlines….moments that quietly change lives. What happened inside the Department of Agrarian Reform this week was one of those moments.

Imagine a long table in Quezon City, filled with people who don’t always share the same politics or priorities. But that morning, they all came together for one reason: the Filipino farmer.

Under the direction of President @bongbongmarcos, the special caucus brought together some of the biggest names in government, including Agriculture Secretary Francisco "Kiko" Tiu Laurel Jr., House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III, Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, and local leaders from the nation’s rice-producing heartlands. It wasn’t a press event or a token meeting. It was a full-blown crisis huddle.

Because while most of us scroll through our feeds, somewhere in Nueva Ecija or Isabela, a farmer is selling his palay at a price barely enough to cover fuel for his tractor. The irony is painful because while the nation depends on them, they can barely depend on the system.

That’s why this caucus matters.

Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said it best: “There is urgency. These are the peak harvest months from October to December, and we must act now to protect our farmers’ livelihoods.”

He emphasized that the meeting was not just another routine consultation but a call to action for the entire government to stand behind the country’s farmers. “Our palay farmers are the backbone of our food security. Under the President’s direction, we are appealing to all government agencies, including GOCCs, to procure rice directly from local producers. Every sack of rice we buy from our own farmers strengthens stability, dignity, and nation-building.”

That message carried weight. It wasn’t mere rhetoric. It was a statement of intent that’s clear, urgent, and deeply human.

Here’s the heart of it: the group will submit a formal recommendation to the President for a policy directive requiring all government offices and GOCCs to prioritize the procurement of locally produced rice.

Think about what that means. Every sack of rice bought locally is more than just a transaction; it is a lifeline. It means a father can send his child to school. A mother can buy better seeds for next season. A community can stay afloat.

This is what #BagongPilipinas looks like in motion: unity that turns compassion into policy.

The President’s call for solidarity within government may not be as loud as a rally speech, but its impact echoes louder where it counts…..sa mga palayan, sa mga barangay, at sa mga tahanan ng mga magsasaka.

For decades, Filipino farmers have been fighting the same battles: low prices, lack of support, and unfair competition. But this time, the government didn’t just issue another promise. It held a caucus that felt more like a commitment….to stand behind those who put food on every Filipino table.

It’s a reminder that real change doesn’t always come with fanfare. Sometimes, it begins with a conversation that turns into action.

And for our farmers, this one might just be the turning point they’ve long prayed for.

LOOK: Campus journalist tagged by PNP as responsible for the violence in the September 21 protest at Mendiola responds to the police through a letter, addressIng the subpeona sent to him on October 7.

Student journalist Jacob Baluyot, associate editor of The Catalyst, the official student publication of the Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP), denied allegations against him by the PNP-CIDG. It named Baluyot as one of the "leaders of the organizations allegedly involved in the violent incident during the Trillion Peso March" on September 21.

According to Baluyot's legal counsel, the subpeona requiring his appearance at the PNP-CIDG investigation already constitutes a custodial investigation, effectively treating Baluyot as a suspect and not a witness.

The College Editors Guild of the Philippines (CEGP) asserted that Baluyot's subpoena adds to a long line of attacks against independent media, including student publications. 

"Journalism is not a crime. The PNP, and the Marcos Jr. administration, must focus on holding corrupt officials accountable rather than intimidating journalists and students who exercise their democratic rights," said CEGP National Spokesperson Brell Lacerna.
